Employee Workplace Policy Manual — 2026
Policy ID: EWP-2026-01 | Version: 2.0 | Status: Approved
Effective Date: 1 April 2026 | Review Date: 31 March 2027
1. Working Hours and Attendance
1.1 Standard Working Hours
The standard working schedule is Monday to Friday, 9:30 AM to 6:00 PM, including a 30-minute lunch
break.
1.2 Flexible Start
Employees may start between 9:00 AM and 10:00 AM with prior manager approval. The employee must
complete the required daily working hours.
1.3 Attendance Correction
An employee must report an attendance-system error to HR within 3 working days of discovering the
error. Requests submitted after this period require HR Head approval.
2. Leave Policy
2.1 Annual Leave
Full-time employees receive 24 days of Annual Leave per calendar year. Leave is credited at the rate of
2 days on the first working day of every month.
2.2 Sick Leave
Employees may take up to 12 days of Sick Leave per calendar year. A medical certificate is required
when Sick Leave exceeds 2 consecutive working days.
2.3 Planned Leave Notice
For planned leave exceeding 3 consecutive working days, employees should submit the leave request
at least 7 calendar days before the first day of leave. Emergency leave is exempt from this notice
requirement.
2.4 Carry Forward
Up to 10 unused Annual Leave days may be carried into the next calendar year. Sick Leave cannot be
carried forward.
3. Remote Work
3.1 Eligibility
Employees who have completed at least 90 days of continuous service may request remote work,
subject to manager approval and role suitability.
3.2 Monthly Limit
Eligible employees may work remotely for up to 8 working days per calendar month. Remote work
cannot be combined with leave to extend an approved leave period without manager approval.
3.3 Equipment
The company may issue a laptop and security accessories to approved remote employees. Employees
are responsible for reasonable care of company equipment.
4. Travel and Reimbursement

[DOC: Employee Workplace Policy Manual | BREADCRUMB: Employee Workplace Policy Manual | PAGE: 2 | CHUNK_ID: IIMA-WORKPLACE-2026_p2_c2]

4.1 Local Travel
Local business travel by personal vehicle may be reimbursed at I8 per kilometre for two-wheelers and
I14 per kilometre for four-wheelers, provided the travel is pre-approved.
4.2 Rail Travel
For approved business travel, standard-class railway fare is reimbursable. Premium or luxury upgrades
require written approval from the Department Head before booking.
4.3 Meal Reimbursement
Employees travelling overnight for official business may claim up to I600 per day for meals. Original
receipts are required for claims above I300.
4.4 Claim Deadline
Travel reimbursement claims must be submitted within 15 calendar days after completion of the trip.

[DOC: Employee Workplace Policy Manual | BREADCRUMB: Employee Workplace Policy Manual | PAGE: 3 | CHUNK_ID: IIMA-WORKPLACE-2026_p3_c3]

5. Internet and Communication
5.1 Home Internet
Employees approved for remote work may claim reimbursement for home broadband charges up to
I1,200 per month. The claim must include the service-provider invoice.
5.2 Mobile Data
Mobile data reimbursement is limited to I500 per month for employees whose role requires business
communication outside the office.
5.3 Scope
Home broadband reimbursement and mobile-data reimbursement are separate benefits. The limit for
one benefit does not increase the limit of the other.
6. Information Security
6.1 Passwords
Company passwords must contain at least 12 characters and must not be shared with another person.
Passwords must be changed immediately if compromise is suspected.
6.2 Public Networks
Employees accessing company systems from public Wi-Fi must use the company-approved VPN.
6.3 Incident Reporting
Suspected security incidents must be reported to the IT Security Team within 2 hours of discovery.
7. Employee Conduct
7.1 Workplace Conduct
Employees are expected to communicate respectfully and maintain professional conduct during working
hours and company activities.
7.2 Conflict of Interest
Employees must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest to HR and their reporting manager
as soon as reasonably possible.
8. Policy Administration
8.1 Approval
This policy is approved by the Human Resources Head and applies from its effective date.
8.2 Exceptions
Exceptions require written approval from the HR Head unless a specific section states a different
approval authority.
8.3 Policy Questions
Where this manual does not provide enough information to answer a question, HR should be consulted.

# Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (IIMA)
## Website Privacy Policy and Terms & Conditions
**Document ID**: IIMA-WEB-PRIVACY-2024 
**Status**: Approved 
**Effective Date**: 2024-01-01 
**Category**: Institutional Digital Governance

### 1. Introduction and Scope
This Privacy Policy and Terms of Use govern the collection, processing, and handling of information collected through the official website of the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (`https://www.iima.ac.in`) and associated public academic portals.

### 2. Information Collection and Processing
1. **Personal Information**: The Institute collects personally identifiable information (such as names, email addresses, phone numbers, and academic qualifications) only when voluntarily submitted by users through application portals, event registrations, or contact forms.
2. **Automated Session Data**: When visitors access the website, web servers automatically log domain names, IP addresses, browser types, operating systems, and page visitation timestamps. This information is utilized solely for statistical aggregation, performance monitoring, and server security analysis.
3. **Cookies**: The website utilizes essential session cookies to preserve user navigation preferences and authentication tokens across secure forms. Cookies do not extract data from the user's hard drive.

### 3. Non-Disclosure & Third-Party Sharing
1. IIMA does not rent, sell, or disclose personal data collected on this website to external third-party commercial organizations.
2. Data may only be shared with governmental, regulatory, or judicial bodies where explicitly mandated under Indian law or statutory court orders.

# Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad
## Executive HR Advisory Committee Memorandum
**Document ID**: IIMA-MEMO-HR-2026-04 
**Date**: 15 May 2026 
**Subject**: Special Addendum on Leave Accumulation Ceilings for Executive & Senior Administrative Cadres 
**Status**: Approved (Internal Governance Memo) 
**Effective Date**: 2026-05-15

### Section 1: Scope & Applicability
This memorandum applies strictly to Senior Administrative Officers (Level 11 and above) and Executive Cadre Staff at the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad.

### Section 2: Modified Accumulation Limits for Earned Leave (EL)
1. Notwithstanding Section 5.2.2 of the Staff HR Policy Manual 2026 (which provides an institutional general ceiling of 300 days), the maximum permissible ceiling on the accumulation of Earned Leave for Executive Cadre Staff covered under this Memorandum shall be restricted to **180 days**.
2. Any Earned Leave standing to the credit of an Executive Cadre employee in excess of 180 days at the close of the calendar year (31st December) shall be automatically converted to cash encashment up to a maximum of 15 days, with the remainder lapsing immediately.
3. This measure is instituted to mitigate accumulated balance sheet liabilities and encourage regular executive rest and recuperation.

### Section 3: Legal Hierarchy & Administrative Precedence
In the event of an interpretive conflict between this Departmental Addendum and the Institute's Gazetted Regulations, the statutory Gazetted Regulations shall supersede. For matters concerning general non-executive staff, the Master Staff HR Policy Manual 2026 remains the sole authoritative baseline.
